Robbins and Cotran.
Where an effective understanding of disease begins.

source delivers that understanding better than the Robbins and Cotran family! Robbins & Kumar Basic Pathology , Robbins
Essential Pathology , and their many companion resources provide a clear, up-to-date explanation of disease
mechanisms you need to succeed.
Robbins & Kumar Basic Pathology, 11th Edition
ISBN: 9780323790185
Key Features:
• Excellent art program boasts high-quality photomicrographs,
gross photos, and radiologic images to supplement the
world-class illustrations.
• Bulleted summary boxes provide quick access to key information and
easy review of key concepts.
• Highlights pathogenesis, morphology, and pathophysiologic
content throughout.
Robbins Essential Pathology, 1st Edition
ISBN: 9780323640251
Key Features:
• T he most concise Robbins text available, providing high-quality content and a
case-based approach in a focused, multimedia learning package for coursework
and exam preparation.
• Focuses on the core knowledge of disease mechanisms and essential clinical
aspects that medical students need to know.
• Features more than 500 images and tables that illustrate key disorders
and concepts.
Explore the entire Robbins and Cotran Family at
elsevierhealth.com/pathology

As we launch the eleventh edition of Pathologic Basis of Disease, it is
worth pausing for a moment to consider the future of pathology as a
discipline and the role of this textbook in the education of twenty-first
century  students.  It  is  apparent  that  an  understanding  of  disease
mechanisms is based more than ever on a strong foundation of basic
science. In turn, new insights have spawned an ever-increasing num-
ber of “targeted therapies” geared to treat disease more effectively and
precisely than in the past. Full understanding of the rationale for these
therapies requires a firm grounding in disease pathophysiology and
relevant basic cellular and molecular biology. To ensure readers have
the necessary knowledge, we have retained and updated our introduc-
tory chapter titled, “The Cell as a Unit of Health and Disease,” and have
woven fundamental aspects of cellular and molecular biology into
discussion of disease throughout this edition.
In the preface of the first edition (1957), Stanley Robbins wrote
“The pathologist is interested not only in the recognition of structural
alterations, but also in their significance, i.e., the effects of these changes
on cellular and tissue function and ultimately the effect of these changes
on the patient. It is not a discipline isolated from the living patient, but
rather a basic approach to a better understanding of disease and there-
fore a foundation of sound clinical medicine.” Here, we have endeavored
to continue to illustrate the principles of pathology that Dr. Robbins
enunciated with such elegance and clarity over half a century ago.
This edition, like all its predecessors, has been extensively revised,
and some areas have been completely rewritten. A few examples of
significant changes are as follows:
•  Chapter 2 has been updated to include novel pathways of cell death
beyond the long-established pathways of necrosis and apoptosis.
Indeed, the distinction between these two is being blurred. Au-
tophagy, which has begun to take center stage in diseases ranging
from aging to cancer and neurodegeneration, has been revised, as
have the possible molecular mechanisms of aging.
•  Chapter 4 has updated information on coagulation pathways, and
current knowledge of sepsis and septic shock
•  Chapter 11 includes a discussion of the pathophysiology of heart
failure with preserved ejection fraction.
•  Chapter 5 (Genetics) includes new discussions of diseases caused
by genetic mosaicism as well as Rett syndrome, a disease of epigen-
etic misprogramming, as well as new approaches to diagnosis, such
as liquid biopsies.
•  Chapter 6 (Immunity) includes an extensively revised and updated
discussion of amyloidosis.
•  Chapter 7 (Cancer) is updated to cover changes in our understand-
ing of cancer pathogenesis and new approaches to molecular diag-
nostics.
•  Chapters 8 (Infectious Disease) and 15 (Lung) have updated dis-
cussions of SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19.
•  Chapter 9 (Environmental Diseases) has expanded coverage of the
role health care disparities play in explaining variation in the inci-
dence and severity of various diseases across different communities
and an updated discussion of obesity, informed by the remarkably
efficacy of GLP-1 agonists.
•  Chapter 11 (Blood Vessels) includes a discussion of the patho-
physiology of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
•  Chapter 18 (Liver) contains updates on the nomenclature, diagnos-
tic criteria, and pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction2associated
viii
steatotic liver disease (MASLD), which continues to increase in
prevalence at an alarming rate in high-resource countries.
•  Chapter 20 (Kidney) has a new discussion of podocytopathies,
particularly minimal change disease, now known to be caused by
autoantibodies against slit diaphragm proteins.
•  Chapter 23 (Breast) has been reorganized to help students better
understand the pathobiology of breast cancer.
•  Chapter 25 (Skin) includes new images demonstrating variation in
the appearance of skin diseases among patients with lighter or
darker skin coloration, alleviating an oversight of previous editions.
•  Chapter 28 (Central Nervous System) has new information about
the pathogenesis of demyelinating and neurodegenerative diseases
and a completely revised classification of brain tumors based on
molecular genetics and morphology, as recommended by interna-
tional committees.
•  Chapter 29 (Eye) has an update on the pathogenesis of age-related
macular degeneration, supported by superb new figures.
•  Chapters 5, 9, 15, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, and 27, covering genetic dis-
eases, environmental diseases, and diseases of the lung, pancreas,
kidney, female genital tract and placenta, breast, endocrine system,
and peripheral nerves and muscle, respectively, all have a fresh look
brought in by new contributors.
•  In addition to the revision and reorganization of the text, many new
photographs and schematic diagrams have been added or revised.
We made the changes highlighted above while remaining focused
on the same longstanding overarching goals, which serve as our guid-
ing principles:
•  To integrate into the discussion of pathologic processes and disor-
ders the newest established information available—morphologic as
well as molecular.
•  To organize information into logical and uniform presentations,
facilitating readability, comprehension, and learning.
•  To maintain the book at a reasonable size and yet provide adequate
discussion of significant lesions, processes, and disorders. Indeed,
despite the addition of new information, the overall length of the
book has decreased by approximately 100 pages. One of our most
challenging tasks is to decide what to eliminate to make room for
key new findings.
•  To place great emphasis on clarity of writing and proper use of
language in the recognition that struggling to comprehend is time-
consuming and wearisome and gets in the way of the learning
process.
•  To make this text useful to students throughout all their years in
medical school and into their residencies—but, at the same time, to
provide sufficient detail and depth to meet the needs of more ad-
vanced readers.
We have repeatedly been told by readers that up-to-datedness is a
special feature that makes this book very valuable. We have strived to
remain current by providing new information from the recent litera-
ture, up to the current year, and by adding coverage of the COVID-19
epidemic.
We now live in a digital age, so an eBook is available to those who
own the print version. Such access gives the reader the ability to search
across the entire text, bookmark passages, add personal notes, use

It is not a discipline isolated from the living patient, but rather a basic approach to a better understanding of disease and therefore a foundation of sound clinical medicine.” Here, we have endeavored to continue to illustrate the principles of pathology that Dr. Robbins enunciated with such elegance and clarity over half a century ago.
This edition, like all its predecessors, has been extensively revised, and some areas have been completely rewritten. A few examples of significant changes are as follows:
•  Chapter 2 has been updated to include novel pathways of cell death beyond the long-established pathways of necrosis and apoptosis.

Indeed, the distinction between these two is being blurred. Autophagy, which has begun to take center stage in diseases ranging from aging to cancer and neurodegeneration, has been revised, as have the possible molecular mechanisms of aging.
•  Chapter 4 has updated information on coagulation pathways, and current knowledge of sepsis and septic shock
•  Chapter 11 includes a discussion of the pathophysiology of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

•  Chapter 5 (Genetics) includes new discussions of diseases caused by genetic mosaicism as well as Rett syndrome, a disease of epigenetic misprogramming, as well as new approaches to diagnosis, such as liquid biopsies.
•  Chapter 6 (Immunity) includes an extensively revised and updated discussion of amyloidosis.
•  Chapter 7 (Cancer) is updated to cover changes in our understanding of cancer pathogenesis and new approaches to molecular diagnostics.
•  Chapters 8 (Infectious Disease) and 15 (Lung) have updated discussions of SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19.

•  Chapter 9 (Environmental Diseases) has expanded coverage of the role health care disparities play in explaining variation in the incidence and severity of various diseases across different communities and an updated discussion of obesity, informed by the remarkably efficacy of GLP-1 agonists.
•  Chapter 11 (Blood Vessels) includes a discussion of the pathophysiology of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
•  Chapter 18 (Liver) contains updates on the nomenclature, diagnostic criteria, and pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction2associated viii
steatotic liver disease (MASLD), which continues to increase in prevalence at an alarming rate in high-resource countries.
•  Chapter 20 (Kidney) has a new discussion of podocytopathies, particularly minimal change disease, now known to be caused by autoantibodies against slit diaphragm proteins.
•  Chapter 23 (Breast) has been reorganized to help students better understand the pathobiology of breast cancer.

•  Chapter 25 (Skin) includes new images demonstrating variation in the appearance of skin diseases among patients with lighter or darker skin coloration, alleviating an oversight of previous editions.

•  Chapter 28 (Central Nervous System) has new information about the pathogenesis of demyelinating and neurodegenerative diseases and a completely revised classification of brain tumors based on molecular genetics and morphology, as recommended by international committees.
•  Chapter 29 (Eye) has an update on the pathogenesis of age-related macular degeneration, supported by superb new figures.

•  Chapters 5, 9, 15, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, and 27, covering genetic diseases, environmental diseases, and diseases of the lung, pancreas, kidney, female genital tract and placenta, breast, endocrine system, and peripheral nerves and muscle, respectively, all have a fresh look brought in by new contributors.
•  In addition to the revision and reorganization of the text, many new photographs and schematic diagrams have been added or revised.
We made the changes highlighted above while remaining focused on the same longstanding overarching goals, which serve as our guiding principles:
•  To integrate into the discussion of pathologic processes and disorders the newest established information available—morphologic as well as molecular.
•  To organize information into logical and uniform presentations, facilitating readability, comprehension, and learning.

•  To maintain the book at a reasonable size and yet provide adequate discussion of significant lesions, processes, and disorders. Indeed, despite the addition of new information, the overall length of the book has decreased by approximately 100 pages. One of our most challenging tasks is to decide what to eliminate to make room for key new findings.

•  To place great emphasis on clarity of writing and proper use of language in the recognition that struggling to comprehend is time-consuming and wearisome and gets in the way of the learning process.

•  To make this text useful to students throughout all their years in medical school and into their residencies—but, at the same time, to provide sufficient detail and depth to meet the needs of more advanced readers.

We have repeatedly been told by readers that up-to-datedness is a special feature that makes this book very valuable. We have strived to remain current by providing new information from the recent literature, up to the current year, and by adding coverage of the COVID-19 epidemic.
